[Thinking]
**Aligning LaTeX Captions**

I'm focusing on left-aligning LaTeX table captions without using the `caption` package. The default centering or justification is proving tricky, so I'm exploring how to override these standard behaviors.

**Redefining LaTeX Caption Logic**

I'm working on manually adjusting LaTeX's captioning mechanism. Specifically, I'm focused on redefining the internal `\@makecaption` command to achieve left alignment without relying on external packages. This involves understanding its current structure and modifying the output logic.
[/Thinking]

To align a table caption to the left in LaTeX without using the `caption` package, you need to redefine the internal LaTeX command `\@makecaption`. 

By default, LaTeX checks if a caption is shorter than one line; if it is, it centers it. If it is longer, it justifies it. Redefining this command allows you to force left-alignment (ragged right) regardless of length.

### Method 1: Global Redefinition (Recommended)
Add this code to your document **preamble** (before `\begin{document}`). 

```latex
\makeatletter
\long\def\@makecaption#1#2{%
  \vskip\abovecaptionskip
  \sbox\@tempboxa{#1: #2}%
  \ifdim \wd\@tempboxa >\hsize
    #1: #2\par
  \else
    \global \@minipagefalse
    \hb@xt@\hsize{#1: #2\hfil}% <--- This line forces left alignment
  \fi
  \vskip\belowcaptionskip}
\makeatother
```

**How it works:**
* `\makeatletter` and `\makeatother` allow you to use the `@` symbol in command names.
* The standard LaTeX behavior uses `\hfil\box\@tempboxa\hfil` to center the box. By changing it to `#1: #2\hfil`, we place the text and push the remaining white space to the right.
* **Note:** This will affect both **Tables** and **Figures**.

---

### Method 2: Local Adjustment (The "Minipage" Trick)
If you only want to align one specific table caption to the left and don't want to change global settings, you can wrap the caption inside a `minipage`.

```latex
\begin{table}[ht]
\centering
\begin{minipage}{\textwidth} % This forces the caption to follow minipage alignment
    \caption{This caption will be aligned to the left of the minipage area.}
\end{minipage}
\begin{tabular}{|c|c|}
\hline
Header 1 & Header 2 \\
\hline
Data 1 & Data 2 \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{table}
```

---

### Method 3: Forcing a "Long" Caption
LaTeX only centers captions that it perceives as "short" (fitting on one line). If you force the caption to take up the full width of the line even if the text is short, it will default to left-alignment (or justification).

You can do this by adding `\hfill` inside the caption:

```latex
\caption{Your caption text here\hfill}
```

*Note: This might result in slightly uneven spacing depending on your document class, but it is the "quickest" fix without CSS-like control.*

---

### Which one should you use?
1. **Method 1** is the professional way to ensure consistency throughout your thesis or paper.
2. **Method 2** is best if you only have one table and don't want to mess with preamble code. 
3. **Method 3** is a "hack" that works in a pinch but is less precise.
